newsitem.title: UK: Boots heads for Japan, Thailand, Netherlands.
newsitem.headline: Boots heads for Japan, Thailand, Netherlands.

text.p: British retailer Boots Co Plc said on Thursday it planned to open health and beauty stores on a pilot basis in Thailand, the Netherlands and Japan and invest about 30 million stg over the next 18 months in the projects.

Boots' deputy chairman and chief executive Lord Blyth and William Heinecke of the Minor Group signed an agreement in Bangkok to form a joint venture and open five Boots stores in Thailand by the summer of 1997, the company said in a statement.
Four stores would be located in the Bangkok area and one store would open in Pattaya.
Three pilot stores would also be opened in the Netherlands in summer 1997, after the company signed a deal with Dutch healthcare provider EVA to provide in-store pharmacy services.
Boots said it would make a further announcement shortly about plans for a trial in Japan.
The company said in June it was investigating international retailing opportunities.

"The purpose of opening these pilot stores is to carry out a thorough evaluation of the commercial opportunities and operational issues before considering the scope for further investment in these countries or elsewhere," Blyth said.
